proof.observed: 43 pages built with every internal link valid; private names clean. A short paragraph now leads: create the secret with its kind from the start, under a name no agent holds a grant on, since a name never served as an ordinary secret has no grant that can release a raw value, so none of what follows applies to it; the gate's list is introduced with 'Where you must convert'. The bullet is split in two: the first says what the second exit 0 establishes and says it of the answering process alone; the second says what no log line will tell you — a peer's reread reads the one name too, so on Secret Manager it can succeed while still reading the old tags, the broker warns only when that read returns an error, and the notification is asynchronous besides, so a healthy peer need not have applied the retag when exit 0 prints. Neither a second exit 0 nor a clean log establishes the peers, named as the residual dispatch://INFRA-375 tracks.

proof.observed: All clean. The stop-path comment no longer says closing the store releases the listener's connection: st.Listener hands pglisten a connection hijacked out of the pool, so st.Close never touches it and what ends the LISTEN is pglisten's own deferred close when its loop returns, which endServing asks for by cancelling serving; the comment says endServing only asks, that nothing waits for that goroutine, and what the order does still buy, which is stopping the reload before st.Close shuts the pool it reads through. main.go:239 and :530-531 and operate.md:416-417 now say the loops run until Shutdown has returned having answered the last request or having spent its 60-second allowance. main.go:588-600, operate.md:363 and :387-390, and AGENTS.md:3034-3037 now say WriteTimeout bounds the exchange after the headers are read rather than every request the server let in, with ReadHeaderTimeout named as what bounds the header read.
proof.negativeControl: My own first draft of this fix was wrong in the same class and was caught by reading rather than recalling: I wrote that Shutdown closes an idle or still-reading connection rather than waiting for it, where net/http's closeIdleConns treats a StateNew connection as idle only after five seconds without headers (its comment cites Go issue 22682). All four copies now say that, which is the fourth claim in this change corrected by going to the source.

trickyParts: The procedure's honest form is not a better gate but a different recommendation. No wording of the gate can establish the peers, because the evidence does not exist: a peer that reads stale tags successfully logs nothing. Leading with 'create the secret with its kind from the start' dissolves the question instead of bounding it, and is the architect's ruling as well as the better text.

The stop path's ordering is right and its account was wrong, which is the harder kind to spot: nothing fails, and the comment reads as an explanation of a dependency that the pool does not actually create. The hijacked connection is the detail that makes the difference, and it is three files away from the comment.
discoveredComplexity: Four sweeps of prose against code, each finding more, is a volume story rather than a carelessness story: a change whose comments outweigh its code has more surface than any one sweep covers. The retro note records the architect's sentence for it — a rule a careful person applies and still misses cases is a rule that needs a smaller surface or a mechanical check — and names the decomposition already on the fast-follow line as the remedy, not a fifth sweep.

Two of this round's corrections were to text this change itself added in the round before, and one was to my own first draft within this round. The error survives whoever is holding the old behaviour in mind; only going to the source each time removes it.
